incident-bot: PagerDuty alert flood — 12 triggers for service=runtime-latency (us-west) at 2026-03-17T20:01:40Z. Auto-resolve in 3m if no new matches. <https://pagerduty.example/INC12345|INC12345>
maya: grabbing this, checking latency/err dashboards now
samir: I can see a sharp CPU blip on the router pool ~20:00, latency spike is short (~15s). No spike in 5xx on the metrics panel
maya: acked on PD and taking lead (maya)
ops-bot: PagerDuty incident INC12345 acknowledged by maya
maya: running quick checks: `kubectl top pod router-01 -n runtime` showed cpu 92% for a minute then back to normal
samir: logs show a burst from a single client IP — looks like a single heavy client session. quick grep snippet: `grep "client_ip" /var/log/requests | tail -n 30` shows repeated long-context requests from 54.23.10.9
carla: any visible customer-facing errors? I'm not seeing elevated 4xx/5xx counts in datadog
maya: confirmed SLOs unaffected, error budget unchanged. No user impact detected
ben: if it's one IP, we can rate-limit at the edge briefly. Want me to add a temporary rule?
maya: holding off on infra changes for now — will mute noisy alerts to stop the page storm and investigate more. muting alert group for 10m, leaving note in PD
samir: created follow-up ticket INC-TUNE-890 to adjust sensitivity and add a rate-based rule plus a check for single-client bursts
maya: handing off monitoring to ben for the next hour. Ben, please escalate to eng-runtime if it repeats or causes errors
ben: taking the handoff — I'll watch the dashboard and PD. If it flares I will open a pager to eng-runtime
ops-bot: PagerDuty incident INC12345 resolved (auto-resolve) at 2026-03-17T20:03:05Z
maya: thanks. marking as no-customer-impact and closing the immediate page. follow-up: tune alert window and add note in runbook about investigating single-client request storms
carla: I'll add the runbook blurb: check client_ip churn, check autoscaler reaction, sample `kubectl top` and request traces
ben: noted. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
maya: TL;DR — transient single-client load caused short router CPU/latency blip, PD fired repeatedly, muted and auto-resolved, no user impact. Follow-up ticket exists to tune alerts and add runbook guidance.
